## Reading-variable construction {#c07-reading-construction}

The reading harmonisation is the most technically involved part of the AFLEARN MICS6 workflow.

The current script is `harmonize-mics-reading-v1.1.R`.

Its purpose is to transform survey-specific reading variables into a consistent child-level file while retaining the information required to understand which language and passage each child was assessed in.

### Pipeline

For each survey:

```text
identify survey
      ↓
repair questionnaire-numbering differences
      ↓
rename reading variables
      ↓
repair known source-data problems
      ↓
identify passage language
      ↓
derive passage length
      ↓
handle second/third passages
      ↓
construct word + comprehension scores
      ↓
construct reading accuracy
      ↓
construct foundational-reading classification
      ↓
classify reading-status pathway
      ↓
retain merge identifiers
```

### Reading score

For a passage:

```text
reading_score =
    words attempted
  - words read incorrectly
```

or:

\[
\text{reading score}
=
\text{words attempted}
-
\text{words incorrect}
\]

The same structure is retained separately for additional passages where relevant.

### Passage language

For single-language surveys, the passage language can be assigned directly.

For multilingual surveys, the language often needs to be inferred using survey-specific combinations of:

- language of instruction;
- home language;
- story selected;
- passage attempted; and
- country questionnaire routing.

This is why `passage_language` is a constructed variable, not merely a renamed questionnaire field.

### Passage length

Reading accuracy requires the number of words in the passage.

The current script derives passage length from the observed source data, generally using the maximum number of words attempted among children assigned to the relevant passage language:

\[
L_l =
\max(\text{words attempted}\mid\text{passage language}=l)
\]

where \(L_l\) is the inferred length of passage language \(l\).

The resulting variable is `passage_length`, with equivalent fields for additional passages.

#### Validation requirement

A data-derived passage length should always be checked.

If no child reaches the end of a passage, the observed maximum can underestimate its true length.

Validation should therefore include:

```text
maximum observed words attempted
questionnaire/story text where available
range of derived reading_accuracy
published survey information
```

A derived accuracy greater than 1 is an immediate warning that passage length or source counts require investigation.

### Reading accuracy

AFLEARN defines:

\[
\text{reading accuracy}
=
\frac{\text{reading score}}
{\text{passage length}}
\]

The output variable is `reading_accuracy`, with passage-specific equivalents where applicable.

### Comprehension

The standard reading assessment contains five comprehension questions.

AFLEARN retains `read_comp_1` through `read_comp_5` and constructs `read_comp_score` as the number answered correctly, conditional on the relevant comprehension sequence having been administered.

Country-specific source-variable mappings are handled before the score is constructed.

### Foundational-reading classification

The current AFLEARN construction combines reading accuracy and comprehension.

The implementation uses the passage-specific integer word cutoff that reproduces the classifications in published MICS outputs.

Where 90% of passage length is not an integer, AFLEARN uses a rounded-down word-count cutoff because validation against published MICS classifications showed that this reproduced the MICS results.

The current implementation is conceptually:

```r
cutoff <- trunc(0.9 * passage_length)

reading_skills =
  reading_score >= cutoff &
  comprehension criterion met
```

This rounding convention is therefore intentional, not a numerical approximation introduced by the guide.

Whenever the reading script is changed, the resulting classifications should again be checked against published country results.

### Multiple passages

A second or third passage is not treated as generic missingness.

The script retains passage-specific variables where needed and builds summary fields such as:

```text
max_reading_score
max_reading_accuracy
max_reading_skills
```

For children with more than one valid attempt, these represent the best observed result across relevant passages.

Researchers should state explicitly when these `max_*` outcomes are used.

### Malawi

Malawi requires special treatment because English and Chichewa are stored as separate passages. Some children attempt only Chichewa.

The script therefore moves Chichewa-only attempts into the primary analysis slots while retaining the passage-language information.

This ensures that the combined reading file contains the complete assessment rather than treating the English passage as if it were the entire Malawi reading sample.

The Malawi MICS 2019–20 questionnaire contains separate English and Chichewa reading pathways, including separate results variables. UNICEF's Malawi reporting also states that the foundational reading assessment was conducted in English and Chichewa.

| Malawi MICS 2019–20 | Number of children |
|---|---:|
| Have `FLWORDSATTEMPT` in an IPUMS extract (English passage) | 1,720 |
| Attempted the Chichewa passage in the original UNICEF data | 3,970 |
| Attempted both passages | 130 |

The original UNICEF source data confirm 3,970 valid observations for `FLB20A`, the number of words attempted in the Chichewa passage. The Malawi questionnaire documentation also shows separate `FL20` and `FL20B` reading-results fields, with `FL20B` corresponding to the Chichewa passage.

Most children who attempted the Chichewa passage have no corresponding value in the IPUMS `FLWORDSATTEMPT` variable. An analysis that treated the IPUMS variable as the Malawi reading sample would therefore omit the Chichewa assessment data.

This is why AFLEARN reconstructs reading from the original UNICEF files rather than from the IPUMS reading variables. See [Getting data from IPUMS MICS](#c01-ipums).

### Practice items

The reading pathway includes a practice sequence.

AFLEARN retains the practice items and constructs `practice_outcome` and `fail_practice`.

These are important because children who fail the practice sequence may never reach the main passage.

A missing main-passage score is therefore not sufficient to distinguish low performance from other assessment pathways.

### `reading_status`

AFLEARN constructs:

| Code | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 0 | Not interviewed |
| 1 | Outside FLS reading age |
| 2 | Caregiver consent not given |
| 3 | Child consent not given |
| 4 | Assessment-language mismatch |
| 5 | Child did not want to read story |
| 6 | Failed practice |
| 7 | Attempted a reading passage |
| 8 | Met foundational-reading criterion |
| 9 | Not classified / inconsistent routing |

The order of assignment matters.

Later observed outcomes overwrite earlier provisional categories where appropriate; code 9 catches observations that remain inconsistent with the expected routing.

The purpose is not just convenience. `reading_status` makes the denominator and assessment pathway visible to analysts.

### Output variables

The research-ready reading file contains, where applicable:

```text
country_iso3
year

HH1
HH2
LN

cluster
hhno
linech

reading_status

passage_language
passage_length

words_att
words_incorrect
reading_score
reading_accuracy

read_comp_1 ... read_comp_5
read_comp_score

practice_*
practice_outcome

reading_skills

passage-B/C equivalents
max_reading_*
```

The technical script remains the authoritative record of the exact processing sequence.
